positive_test: partitions or groups unlabelled points without any target variable
negative_test: grouping by a supplied label
examples: k-means, DBSCAN, Ward linkage

name: Centroid-based clustering
positive_test: assigns points to the nearest of k representatives and updates the representatives
negative_test: growing clusters by density connectivity or by merging
examples: k-means, k-means++, mini-batch k-means, k-medoids/PAM, fuzzy c-means

name: Hierarchical clustering
positive_test: builds a nested merge or split tree under a linkage criterion
negative_test: producing a flat partition with a fixed k
examples: agglomerative clustering, single/complete/average/Ward linkage, divisive clustering

name: Density-based clustering
positive_test: defines clusters as connected regions above a density threshold
negative_test: assuming a fixed number of convex clusters
examples: DBSCAN, OPTICS, HDBSCAN, mean-shift

name: Mixture-model clustering
positive_test: fits a probabilistic mixture and assigns soft responsibilities
negative_test: assigning hard memberships by distance
examples: Gaussian mixture models, Bayesian GMM, Dirichlet-process mixtures, latent class analysis

name: Graph and spectral clustering
positive_test: clusters using the eigenstructure or modularity of a similarity or adjacency graph
negative_test: clustering directly in feature space
examples: spectral clustering, normalised cuts, affinity propagation, Louvain, Leiden

name: Dimensionality reduction and factorisation
characteristic: what structure of the data the low-dimensional map preserves
positive_test: produces a lower-dimensional representation of the data with no target variable
negative_test: predicting a target from features
examples: PCA, t-SNE, UMAP, NMF
notes: many of these produce no separable model

name: Variance-preserving projections
positive_test: finds orthogonal directions maximising retained variance or minimising reconstruction error
negative_test: preserving pairwise distances or neighbourhoods
examples: PCA, probabilistic PCA, sparse PCA, kernel PCA, randomised SVD, incremental PCA

name: Independent-component decomposition
positive_test: finds a linear basis whose coefficients are maximally statistically independent
negative_test: finding a basis that is merely uncorrelated
examples: FastICA, Infomax ICA, JADE, SOBI

name: Parts-based and topic factorisation
positive_test: factorises with non-negativity or a generative topic prior so components are additive parts
negative_test: allowing arbitrary signed loadings
examples: NMF, sparse NMF, PLSA, latent Dirichlet allocation, dictionary learning
notes: LDA here is the topic model, not the discriminant

name: Neighbourhood-preserving embedding
positive_test: places points so that local neighbourhood structure is preserved in low dimensions
negative_test: maximising global variance
examples: MDS, Isomap, LLE, Laplacian eigenmaps, t-SNE, UMAP, PaCMAP, TriMap
notes: t-SNE produces coordinates, not a reusable model

name: Supervised and multi-view projections
positive_test: finds directions that maximise class separation or cross-view correlation
negative_test: ignoring labels and second views
examples: Fisher LDA, CCA, kernel CCA, deep CCA, PLS regression

name: Random projection and sketching
positive_test: projects with a random matrix whose distortion is bounded in expectation
negative_test: fitting the projection to the data
examples: Johnson-Lindenstrauss projection, sparse random projection, CountSketch, random SVD sketching

name: Matrix completion and collaborative factorisation
positive_test: factorises a partially observed matrix to predict its missing entries
negative_test: factorising a fully observed matrix for representation
examples: ALS matrix factorisation, SVD++, soft-impute, nuclear-norm completion

name: State-space and structured sequence inference
characteristic: what state representation inference runs over
positive_test: infers a latent sequence or its parameters under an explicit temporal model
negative_test: fitting an unstructured sequence model with no latent-state semantics
examples: HMM, Kalman filter, CRF

name: Discrete-state sequence inference
positive_test: runs forward-backward or Viterbi recursions over a discrete latent chain
negative_test: assuming a continuous Gaussian state
examples: forward-backward, Baum-Welch, Viterbi, HSMM

name: Gaussian state-space filtering
positive_test: propagates a Gaussian belief through linear or linearised dynamics
negative_test: representing the belief by particles
examples: Kalman filter, EKF, UKF, RTS smoother, information filter

name: Sequential Monte Carlo
positive_test: represents the belief by weighted particles that are resampled over time
negative_test: maintaining a closed-form Gaussian belief
examples: particle filter, auxiliary particle filter, SMC, SMC-squared, particle MCMC

name: Discriminative structured prediction
positive_test: models the conditional distribution over label sequences with global normalisation
negative_test: modelling the joint distribution of observations and labels
examples: MEMM, linear-chain CRF, structured perceptron, structured SVM

name: Classical time-series forecasting
positive_test: fits an explicit autoregressive, trend and seasonality decomposition
negative_test: fitting a generic neural sequence model
examples: ARIMA, SARIMA, exponential smoothing, Holt-Winters, Prophet, structural time series, VAR

name: Graph algorithms as learning procedures
characteristic: what is propagated across the graph
positive_test: computes a quantity by propagating along a graph's edges to convergence
negative_test: computing from feature vectors without a graph
examples: PageRank, belief propagation, Louvain, Weisfeiler-Lehman kernel, shortest paths

name: Resampling-based inference
characteristic: what is resampled and for what estimate
positive_test: re-fits an estimator on resampled data to quantify variability or select a model
negative_test: computing an analytic standard error
examples: bootstrap, jackknife, permutation test, k-fold cross-validation

name: Resampling confidence estimation
positive_test: builds intervals or standard errors from the distribution of resampled estimates
negative_test: building intervals from an asymptotic formula
examples: bootstrap, BCa bootstrap, block bootstrap, jackknife, bootstrap-t

name: Cross-validation
positive_test: partitions data into folds and averages held-out performance to select or assess
negative_test: evaluating once on a single held-out split
examples: k-fold CV, stratified CV, leave-one-out, nested CV, time-series CV, group CV
notes: admissible only if evaluation is in scope; see Tensions

name: Permutation and randomisation tests
positive_test: builds a null distribution by permuting labels or group assignment
negative_test: assuming a parametric null distribution
examples: permutation test, randomisation test, permutation feature importance

name: Markov-chain Monte Carlo
characteristic: how proposals are generated
positive_test: draws correlated samples from a target density via a Markov chain with the right stationary law
negative_test: optimising a parametric approximation to the posterior
examples: Metropolis-Hastings, Gibbs, HMC, NUTS

name: Metropolis-Hastings family
positive_test: proposes from an arbitrary kernel and accepts with the Metropolis ratio
negative_test: sampling each coordinate from its exact conditional
examples: Metropolis, Metropolis-Hastings, random-walk MH, adaptive MH, MALA

name: Gibbs sampling
positive_test: samples each block from its exact full conditional, always accepting
negative_test: using an accept-reject step
examples: Gibbs sampling, collapsed Gibbs, blocked Gibbs, slice sampling

name: Gradient-informed samplers
positive_test: uses the gradient of the log density to propose distant, high-acceptance moves
negative_test: proposing without derivative information
examples: Langevin/MALA, HMC, NUTS, SGLD, SGHMC, Riemannian HMC
notes: SGLD bridges to stochastic optimisation

name: Tempered and annealed sampling
positive_test: runs chains at multiple temperatures or anneals between distributions
negative_test: a single chain at a fixed target
examples: parallel tempering, simulated tempering, annealed importance sampling, SMC samplers

name: Evidence-oriented sampling
positive_test: targets the marginal likelihood by sampling nested likelihood shells
negative_test: targeting posterior expectations only
examples: nested sampling, MultiNest, dynamic nested sampling
notes: speculative in ML venues; standard in astrostatistics

name: Variational inference
characteristic: what family and bound are used
positive_test: approximates a posterior by optimising a divergence over a tractable family
negative_test: drawing samples from the exact posterior
examples: mean-field VI, CAVI, SVI, ADVI, black-box VI, expectation propagation
notes: parent of the VAE lineage

name: Likelihood-based point estimation
characteristic: what is maximised or matched
positive_test: selects parameters by maximising a likelihood or matching moments
negative_test: producing a full posterior distribution
examples: MLE, MAP, penalised likelihood, partial likelihood (Cox), method of moments, generalised method of moments, M-estimation
notes: note the GMM name collision with Gaussian mixtures

name: Hypothesis testing and error control
characteristic: what is being controlled
positive_test: computes a test statistic and a decision rule with a stated error rate
negative_test: reporting an effect size with no decision rule
examples: t-test, ANOVA, Mann-Whitney, chi-square, Bonferroni, Holm, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR
notes: admissible only if evaluation is in scope

name: Causal effect estimation
characteristic: what source of identification the estimator leans on
positive_test: estimates an interventional or counterfactual contrast under a stated identification assumption
negative_test: estimating a predictive association with no identification claim
examples: propensity score matching, doubly robust estimation, difference-in-differences

name: Adjustment and weighting estimators
positive_test: identifies the effect by conditioning on or reweighting by observed confounders
negative_test: using an instrument or a discontinuity
examples: g-computation, propensity score matching, IPW, AIPW/doubly robust, TMLE, double ML, entropy balancing

name: Instrumental-variable estimation
positive_test: uses a variable affecting treatment but not the outcome except through treatment
negative_test: adjusting for measured confounders only
examples: 2SLS, LIML, GMM-IV, deep IV, Mendelian randomisation

name: Panel and design-based estimators
positive_test: identifies from repeated observation of the same units before and after treatment
negative_test: identifying from cross-sectional variation
examples: difference-in-differences, event study, synthetic control, synthetic DiD, two-way fixed effects

name: Discontinuity designs
positive_test: identifies from assignment determined by a threshold in a running variable
negative_test: identifying from random or conditionally random assignment
examples: sharp regression discontinuity, fuzzy RD, kink designs

name: Heterogeneous-effect estimation
positive_test: estimates how the effect varies with covariates, not only its average
negative_test: estimating a single average treatment effect
examples: causal forest, S/T/X-learner, DR-learner, uplift modelling, BART for causal effects

name: Causal structure discovery
positive_test: infers the graph of causal relations rather than an effect size given a graph
negative_test: estimating an effect from an assumed graph
examples: PC, FCI, GES, NOTEARS, LiNGAM, DAG-GNN, CCM

name: Representation-based counterfactual estimation
positive_test: learns a representation balancing treated and control groups and predicts both potential outcomes
negative_test: using a fixed propensity model with no learned representation
examples: TARNet, CFR/IPM-balanced representations, Dragonnet, CEVAE, GANITE

name: Anomaly and outlier detection
characteristic: what makes a point anomalous
positive_test: scores points by how unusual they are, typically fitted without anomaly labels
negative_test: classifying points against labelled anomaly classes
examples: isolation forest, one-class SVM, LOF

name: Density-based anomaly scoring
positive_test: scores by estimated density or local density ratio
negative_test: scoring by a learned decision boundary
examples: KDE scoring, LOF, GMM likelihood scoring, COPOD

name: Boundary-based anomaly scoring
positive_test: fits a compact boundary around the normal data and scores by distance outside
negative_test: estimating a density
examples: one-class SVM, SVDD, Deep SVDD

name: Isolation and partition scoring
positive_test: scores by how few random splits are needed to isolate a point
negative_test: fitting a density or a boundary
examples: isolation forest, extended isolation forest, RRCF

name: Reconstruction-error anomaly scoring
positive_test: scores by how badly a generative or autoencoding model reconstructs the point
negative_test: scoring by an explicit density estimate
examples: autoencoder reconstruction error, VAE ELBO scoring, diffusion reconstruction scoring

name: Change-point and sequence anomalies
positive_test: detects a shift in a temporal process rather than a point outlier
negative_test: flagging individual independent points
examples: CUSUM, Bayesian online change-point detection, PELT, matrix profile

name: Recommendation and ranking procedures
characteristic: what the ranking signal is fitted to
positive_test: fits a model to produce an ordering over items for a user or query
negative_test: predicting an unordered label
examples: ALS collaborative filtering, BPR, LambdaMART

name: Collaborative filtering
positive_test: predicts preferences from the interaction matrix alone
negative_test: using item or query content features
examples: user-kNN and item-kNN CF, ALS, SVD++, BPR, neural CF

name: Learning to rank
positive_test: optimises a listwise or pairwise ranking loss against relevance judgements
negative_test: optimising a pointwise regression loss
examples: RankNet, LambdaRank, LambdaMART, ListNet, ListMLE

name: Discrete optimisation inside learning
characteristic: what combinatorial structure is solved
positive_test: solves a combinatorial subproblem as a step inside a learning procedure
negative_test: solving a continuous parameter optimisation
examples: Hungarian matching, Sinkhorn, Viterbi, beam search as search
notes: underrated: appears inside many deep pipelines

name: Assignment and matching
positive_test: solves a bipartite matching to pair predictions with targets or clusters
negative_test: sorting or thresholding heuristically
examples: Hungarian algorithm, DETR bipartite matching, auction algorithm

name: Optimal transport
positive_test: computes a coupling minimising transport cost between two distributions
negative_test: computing a pointwise divergence
examples: Sinkhorn-Knopp, entropic OT, Wasserstein distance, Gromov-Wasserstein, SwAV assignment step

name: Greedy submodular selection
positive_test: selects a set greedily under a submodular objective with an approximation guarantee
negative_test: selecting by independent per-item score
examples: facility location coresets, greedy maximum coverage, k-center greedy

name: Exact combinatorial solvers
positive_test: solves to optimality with branch and bound or an integer program
negative_test: using a heuristic with no optimality claim
examples: branch and bound, mixed-integer programming, constraint programming, SAT-based learning

name: Constraint- and physics-informed fitting
characteristic: what known structure is imposed
positive_test: adds a known equation, conservation law or logical constraint as part of the objective
negative_test: learning the relationship purely from data
examples: PINN, Lagrangian/Hamiltonian neural network training, SINDy, Deep Ritz

name: Symbolic regression
characteristic: how the expression space is searched
positive_test: searches over symbolic expressions for one that fits the data
negative_test: fitting coefficients of a fixed functional form
examples: genetic symbolic regression, SINDy, AI Feynman, neural-guided symbolic regression
notes: partly speculative in mainstream ML venues
